..
Current visible satellite imagery depicts the Marianas in a dry, 
diffusive pattern following a very weak trade-wind trough 
downstream. Earlier this morning, small areas of moderate convection
and isolated thunderstorms were seen far NE of Saipan and ESE of 
Guam. However, both areas have been reduced to lingering cirrus, 
supporting the isolated shower regime at least through tonight. Due 
to the slowing and divergence of the overall surface flow, winds 
will become light and variable tonight, returning to the usual 10 to 
15 mph easterly trades shortly after sunrise. This pattern will 
persist through at least midweek. Forecaster confidence is still low 
regarding Invest 92W (see Tropical Systems section below) as the 
different model groups disagree from each other. Therefore, PoPs were
kept at 30 percent for the last few periods of the forecast. Whether
or not this system impacts the Marianas will greatly depend on its 
evolution for the next several days.

Marine...
Light to gentle east winds will persist for marine areas through
midweek. The current east swell may build, increasing combined seas
from 2 to 3 ft to 3 to 4 ft around Monday. The latter half may see
combined seas up to 5 ft, but that is dependent on Invest 92W as it
would be the main driver for that increase in swell. A low risk of
rip currents will continue through at least the weekend. Island
heating has caused a build up in showers over western coastal waters
in the late afternoon through early evening. This pattern is 
expected to persist for the next few days, so wording was added in 
the forecast.

Tropical Systems...
A weak tropical disturbance, Joint Typhoon Warning Center's (JTWC)
Invest 92W, is centered southeast of Majuro near 6.4N 172.4E along 
the east end of the Near-Equatorial Trough (NET). 92W remains sub-
low, meaning development is not expected within the next couple of 
days. The invest has moved slowly west-northwest over the past 24 
hours and remains fairly disorganized. 92W is expected to slowly 
drift west or west-northwest over the next few days with little to 
no strengthening expected into the beginning of next week. The slow 
movement will maintain convection across the Marshall Islands through
the first half of next week. Invest 92W will be monitored closely 
over the next few days for signs of strengthening. 

Eastern Micronesia...
The NET and Invest 92W remain the primary mechanisms in eastern
Micronesia this afternoon. Invest 92W has moved a little farther
west-northwest and is now centered southeast of Majuro near 6N172E.
Convection has increased across the Marshalls, with numerous showers
and isolated thunderstorms present south of Jaluit northward to 
around 12N. Based on satellite trends and in opposition of the 
latest model data, increased POPs (Probability of Precipitation) to 
60 percent, going from scattered to numerous showers, with isolated 
thunderstorms. Convection will be very slow to move out of the 
Marshalls as Invest 92W maintains a slow movement west-northwest 
over the next few days. As 92W moves west-northwest, it will drag 
the NET along with it. This is now expected to pull increased 
convection into Kosrae and Pohnpei by the middle of next week as the 
NET drifts north. Otherwise, the dry pattern looks to continue at 
both Pohnpei and Kosrae until this occurs.

For the marine forecast, no major changes were made, with mostly
light to gentle winds throughout the region continuing through
midweek next week along with seas between 3 and 5 feet.

Western Micronesia...
For Palau and Yap, the models continue to show a dry pattern,
unfortunately, with just isolated showers expected. With that said,
the NET (Near-Equatorial Trough) is located just south of Koror and 
if convection is strong enough to generate an outflow boundary moving
northeast, that with orographic lift could locally increase rainfall
potential. However, this looks like a remote possibility at best.

For Chuuk, it's relatively "status quo" through Wednesday morning, as
a lack of surface features will keep shower coverage limited to
isolated. Then, as we head into Wednesday night and Thursday, a
slowly-developing tropical system may pass by to the north. 
Depending how close it is, a monsoon-like southwesterly flow into it 
could increase rainfall potential starting on Thursday. Stay tuned!

As for marine conditions, mariners can expect light to gentle winds 
and seas of 3 to 5 feet through the forecast period.
